Bisher erhaltene Abrechnungen der Leistungserbringer und/oder deren Dienstleistern, die in Papierform eingehen, sollen durch den Auftragnehmer digitalisiert und so der Auftraggeberin zur Verfügung gestellt werden. Dadurch erleichtert sich für die Auftraggeberin die Rechnungs- bearbeitung und es wird Potenzial für Prozessoptimierungen und -automatisierungen geschaf- fen. Details sind der Leistungsbeschreibung zu entnehmen. 1.1 Losbildung Eine Losbildung unterbleibt, da ein ganzheitlicher Scandienst mit der Gesamtverantwortung des künftigen Auftragnehmers ausgeschrieben wird. Ausgeschrieben wird ein Rahmenvertrag mit einem Wirtschaftsteilnehmer. Bieter sind aufgefordert, ein Angebot einzureichen. 1.2 Art der Vergabe Die Auftraggeberin schreibt die benötigten Leistungen in einem offenen Verfahren im Sinne von § 15 VgV aus. Dieses Vergabeverfahren wird aus Gründen der Transparenz über eine elektronische Vergabeplattform betrieben. Die Auftraggeberin verwendet ausschließ lich die Vergabeplattform der DTVP Deutsches Vergabeportal GmbH (www.dtvp.de). Es ist das zum Zeitpunkt der Veröffentlichung der Bekanntmachung geltende Vergaberecht maßgeblich, auch, wenn dieses sich während des Vergabeverfahrens ändern sollte. Täitja kohustub oma kulul esindama tellijat lepingu alusel täidetavate ülesannete või toimingutega seotud kõigis vaidlustes (sh kohtuvaidlustes) kolmandate isikutega ning kandma kõik sellega kaasnevad menetluskulud. 7.7 Tellija võib lepingu üles öelda, kui Täitja rikub oluliselt õigusaktidest või lepingust tulenevaid kohustusi. When: Within ninety (90) calendar days from the date of contract award. Where: American Center, U.S. Consulate General Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. Why: To modernize the Center's technological capability with high-end American brand /equivalent hardware that projects a premium, high-tech "American look and

ling flawless technical delivery for public diplomacy programming. Goal: Deploy flexible, multi-modal AV and computing infrastructure that supports formal briefings, large public events, and STEM/makerspace programming. Target Audience: Guests of U.S. Consulate General Chennai, VIP/ executive stakeholders, technical teams, and American Center program attendees & visitors. Primary Objective: Deliver fully tested, IT-cleared, American brand / equivalent technology hardware. All hardware selections are subject to final U.S. Government and Consulate IT team clearance prior to purchase. SECTION B: KEY COMPONENTS & SCOPE B.1 Primary Digital Wall - Quantity 1, Supply, configure, and mount a high-definition digital video wall measuring approximately 10 ft (H) × 10 ft (W). B.2 Interactive Smart Board Supply and install one (1) commercial-grade interactive smart board for digital brainstorming, real-time notation, and schematic illustration. The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and proc

ISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performanc

sociated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.

f_Work.docx ===== STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) RFID Cabinet The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires the acquisition of a Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) storage cabinet integrated with Unique Device Identifier (UDI)-compliant tissue and implant tracking software to support patient safety, regulatory compliance, and efficient inventory management. Tracking tissues, biologics, and implantable medical devices is a federal regulatory requirement under FDA 21 CFR Part 830 (UDI) and is critical to patient safety. VA healthcare facilities face ongoing resource challenges including staff shortages and budget constraints, making it essential to minimize staff time consumed by manual data entry and to maintain precise control over high-value inventory. This acquisition will provide an automated, real-time RFID-based inventory management solution for use in the operating room (OR), Catheterization (Cath) lab, ambulatory surgery center, or any facility location that stores high-value implantable inventory.
